name: Node & pod affinity
objective: CKA › Workloads & Scheduling. Drill EVERY way to control where pods land, harder than the exam: node labels + nodeSelector, taints & tolerations (Equal + Exists), required and preferred nodeAffinity, pod anti-affinity spread, manual nodeName scheduling, DaemonSet coverage, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix for an unschedulable pod. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Required nodeAffinity (In operator)
questions.teach:
**nodeAffinity** (`spec.affinity.nodeAffinity`) is a richer nodeSelector using `matchExpressions` with operators `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, `Gt`, `Lt`. The **hard** form `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` must be satisfied or the pod stays `Pending`.

**Gotcha:** affinity attracts but doesn't defeat taints — since `$W1` is now tainted, this pod also needs a toleration.
questions.prompt:
Node `$W1` is labeled `tier=gold`. In `sched-learn` create pod `affinity-pod` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) using **required** nodeAffinity matching `tier In [gold]`, tolerating any taint so it can land on `$W1`.

Target: `affinity-pod` is `Running` on the `tier=gold` node via required nodeAffinity.
questions.hint: Under `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms[0].matchExpressions[0]` set `key: tier`, `operator: In`, `values: [gold]`. Add `tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: affinity-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
          - key: tier
            operator: In
            values: ["gold"]
  tolerations:
  - operator: Exists
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: affinity-pod Running on tier=gold node via required nodeAffinity

questions.eli5:
Think of the cluster as a neighbourhood and your pod as a family looking for a house (a node). A plain `nodeSelector` is like saying "only a house with a blue door." **nodeAffinity** is the upgraded version of that wish list — it can say much smarter things.

`nodeAffinity` lets you match on a *set* of values, not just one exact value: "any house whose `tier` label is **one of** gold, platinum" (the `In` operator). It can also say `NotIn`, "the label just has to exist" (`Exists`), or even compare numbers (`Gt`/`Lt`).

The flavour you use here is the **hard** one with the long name `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`. "Required" means it's a firm rule: no matching house, no move-in — the pod sits `Pending` forever, exactly like a `nodeSelector` that matches nothing.

The one trick to burn into memory: **affinity only attracts, it never barges past a locked door.** If the house you want has a "Keep Out" sign (a **taint**), wanting it isn't enough — you still need a matching pass (a **toleration**). That's why this pod carries a toleration too.

**Watch out:**

- **Required affinity = `Pending` if nothing matches.** Check `kubectl describe pod` → Events → "didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector."
- **Affinity does not defeat taints.** The gold node is tainted, so the pod also needs a `toleration` or it still won't land.
- The long field name is **`requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`** — "IgnoredDuringExecution" means once the pod is running, changing node labels won't evict it.
- `values:` is a **list**, even for one value: `values: ["gold"]`.
- Multiple `nodeSelectorTerms` are OR'ed; multiple `matchExpressions` inside one term are AND'ed. Easy to mix up.
questions.deepDive:
## Required nodeAffinity — full rundown ### The one-sentence model **nodeAffinity is nodeSelector with operators and set logic.** The *required* (hard) form must be satisfied or the pod stays `Pending`; it attracts a pod to matching nodes but, like all attraction rules, it does **not** defeat taints. ### Where it lives ```yaml spec: affinity: nodeAffinity: requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: nodeSelectorTerms: - matchExpressions: - key: tier operator: In values: ["gold"] ``` ### The two forms | Field | Hard/soft | If nothing matches | |---|---|---| | `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` | **hard** | pod stays `Pending` | | `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` | soft | pod schedules anywhere | - **During Scheduling** — the rule is evaluated when the pod is being placed. - **IgnoredDuringExecution** — once running, relabelling the node does **not** evict the pod. (There is no `RequiredDuringExecution` form yet.) ### Operators | Operator | Meaning | `values` required? | |---|---|---| | `In` | label value is one of the listed values | yes (≥1) | | `NotIn` | label value is **not** any listed value | yes | | `Exists` | the key exists (any value) | **no** — omit `values` | | `DoesNotExist` | the key is absent | **no** | | `Gt` | value > the single integer given | yes (one integer) | | `Lt` | value < the single integer given | yes (one integer) | `NotIn` / `DoesNotExist` give you **node anti-affinity** (keep off certain nodes). ### AND vs OR — the critical nesting rule - `nodeSelectorTerms` is a **list**; terms are **OR-ed** (any one term satisfied → node qualifies). - Within a single term, all `matchExpressions` are **AND-ed** (every expression must match). ```yaml requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: nodeSelectorTerms: - matchExpressions: # term 1 (tier=gold AND zone=a) - {key: tier, operator: In, values: ["gold"]} - {key: zone, operator: In, values: ["a"]} - matchExpressions: # OR term 2 (tier=platinum) - {key: tier, operator: In, values: ["platinum"]} ``` ### nodeSelector vs nodeAffinity | | nodeSelector | nodeAffinity | |---|---|---| | Match style | exact `key=value`, AND-ed | operators + sets | | Soft/preferred option | ❌ | ✅ (`preferred…`) | | OR logic | ❌ | ✅ (multiple terms) | | Negation (`NotIn`) | ❌ | ✅ | Both are **attraction only** and both ignore taints. ### Affinity + taints together A node can be *labelled* (attracts) and *tainted* (repels) at once. To land on it you need **both** a matching affinity/selector **and** a matching toleration: ```yaml spec: affinity: nodeAffinity: requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: nodeSelectorTerms: - matchExpressions: - {key: tier, operator: In, values: ["gold"]} tolerations: - operator: Exists # tolerate every taint ``` ### Gotchas & exam traps - **Nothing matches → `Pending`.** `kubectl describe pod

` → Events → *"0/N nodes are available: N node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector."* - **Affinity never beats a taint.** Tainted target node also needs a toleration. - **`values` must be a YAML list**, even for a single value: `values: ["gold"]`. - **`Exists`/`DoesNotExist` must NOT carry `values`** — including them is a validation error. - **OR vs AND nesting**: separate `nodeSelectorTerms` entries = OR; multiple `matchExpressions` in one = AND. Mixing these up is the #1 affinity mistake. - **Immutable after creation**: you can't edit a running pod's affinity — recreate it (or fix the Deployment template). - `IgnoredDuringExecution`: relabelling a node later will **not** move an already-running pod. ### Quick reference ```yaml spec: affinity: nodeAffinity: requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: nodeSelectorTerms: - matchExpressions: - {key: tier, operator: In, values: ["gold"]} tolerations: - {operator: Exists} ``` ```bash kubectl get nodes -L tier # confirm which node is tier=gold kubectl get pod affinity-pod -o wide # NODE == the tier=gold node kubectl describe pod affinity-pod | sed -n '/Events/,$p' ```

questions.title: Preferred nodeAffinity (soft, weighted)
questions.teach:
The **soft** form `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` is a *preference*, not a rule: each entry has a `weight` (1–100) and a `preference` term. The scheduler favors matching nodes but still schedules elsewhere if none match.

**Gotcha:** preferred affinity never leaves a pod `Pending` — if no node matches it just lands somewhere else, so you can't rely on it for a hard placement requirement.
questions.prompt:
In `sched-learn` create pod `prefer-pod` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) that **prefers** (weight `80`) nodes labeled `zone=b`, tolerating any taint. Node `$W2` is labeled `zone=b`.

Target: `prefer-pod` is `Running` and declares a `preferredDuringScheduling` nodeAffinity entry of weight `80` matching `zone In [b]`.
questions.hint: `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: [{weight: 80, preference: {matchExpressions: [{key: zone, operator: In, values: [b]}]}}]`; add `tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: prefer-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 80
        preference:
          matchExpressions:
          - key: zone
            operator: In
            values: ["b"]
  tolerations:
  - operator: Exists
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: prefer-pod Running with preferred nodeAffinity weight 80, zone In [b]

questions.eli5:
Imagine booking a hotel room through an app. A **required** rule is "I will ONLY take a sea-view room" — if none exist, you don't book at all. A **preferred** rule is "I'd *love* a sea-view room, but if there isn't one, just give me whatever's free." You still get a room either way.

That's `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`: a **soft wish**, not a hard rule. Each wish has a **weight** from 1 to 100 — think of it as how many stars you'd give that preference. The scheduler adds up the weights of all the preferences a node satisfies and sends the pod to the highest-scoring node. A higher weight = a stronger nudge, but never a guarantee.

Here you ask for nodes labeled `zone=b` with weight `80` — a strong nudge toward the `zone=b` node. If that node is available and nothing outweighs it, the pod lands there. If it's full or missing, the pod simply lands elsewhere — **it never waits.**

**Watch out:**

- **Preferred never causes `Pending`.** If no node matches, the pod schedules somewhere else anyway. Never use preferred when you *require* a specific placement — use the required form for that.
- The structure differs from required: preferred is a **list of `{weight, preference}` objects**, and the term is spelled `preference` (not `nodeSelectorTerms`). Easy to swap by accident.
- **weight must be 1–100.** It's only a tie-breaker between candidate nodes, not an absolute rule.
- On a tiny cluster the nudge can look like it "didn't work" — other factors (spreading, resources) may outweigh an 80. That's normal.
- Like all affinity, it **ignores taints** — a tainted preferred node still needs a toleration to be usable.
questions.deepDive:
## Preferred (soft) nodeAffinity — full rundown

### The one-sentence model
**Preferred nodeAffinity is a weighted wish, not a rule.** The scheduler *scores* nodes by how many preferences they satisfy and places the pod on the best-scoring node — but if nothing matches, the pod still schedules somewhere. It can **never** leave a pod `Pending`.

### Where it lives
```yaml
spec:
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 80
        preference:
          matchExpressions:
          - key: zone
            operator: In
            values: ["b"]
```

### Required vs preferred — structure differs
| | required | preferred |
|---|---|---|
| Field | `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` | `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` |
| Shape | object with `nodeSelectorTerms:` (list of terms) | **list** of `{weight, preference}` |
| Inner term key | `nodeSelectorTerms[].matchExpressions` | `preference.matchExpressions` |
| Has `weight`? | ❌ | ✅ (1–100, required) |
| No match → | pod `Pending` | pod schedules elsewhere |

> Common mistake: writing `nodeSelectorTerms` under the preferred form, or forgetting the `preference:` wrapper. The preferred inner term is `preference`, a single term (not a list of terms).

### How weight works
- Each preferred entry has a `weight` in **1–100**.
- During scoring, every node that satisfies a given entry gets that entry's weight added to its score.
- Node with the **highest total score** wins. Multiple preferred entries stack.
- Weight is relative — it competes with other scheduler scoring (resource balancing, pod spreading, image locality). A single `weight: 80` is a strong nudge but not absolute.

```yaml
preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
- weight: 80
  preference:
    matchExpressions:
    - {key: zone, operator: In, values: ["b"]}
- weight: 20
  preference:
    matchExpressions:
    - {key: disktype, operator: In, values: ["ssd"]}
```
A node that is `zone=b` **and** `ssd` scores 100; `zone=b` only scores 80; neither scores 0.

### Operators
Same set as required nodeAffinity: `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, `DoesNotExist`, `Gt`, `Lt`. (`Exists`/`DoesNotExist` take no `values`.)

### Combining required + preferred
You can use both at once: required narrows the eligible set (or nothing lands), preferred ranks within it.
```yaml
nodeAffinity:
  requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    nodeSelectorTerms:
    - matchExpressions:
      - {key: disktype, operator: In, values: ["ssd"]}
  preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
  - weight: 80
    preference:
      matchExpressions:
      - {key: zone, operator: In, values: ["b"]}
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Preferred never → `Pending`.** If a task says "must land on X," that's the *required* form, not preferred.
- **`weight` is mandatory** on each preferred entry and must be **1–100** (0 is invalid).
- **Wrong inner key**: preferred uses `preference:` (singular term), required uses `nodeSelectorTerms:` (list). Don't swap them.
- **`IgnoredDuringExecution`**: relabelling after scheduling won't move a running pod.
- **Still ignores taints**: a preferred-but-tainted node needs a matching toleration to even be a candidate.
- On small clusters the nudge may be outweighed by other scoring — don't treat it as a guarantee of placement.

### Verify what the pod declares
```bash
kubectl get pod prefer-pod -o jsonpath='{.spec.affinity.nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution}'; echo
kubectl get pod prefer-pod -o wide
```

### Quick reference
```yaml
spec:
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 80
        preference:
          matchExpressions:
          - {key: zone, operator: In, values: ["b"]}
  tolerations:
  - {operator: Exists}
```

questions.title: Pod anti-affinity (spread across nodes)
questions.teach:
**podAntiAffinity** keeps pods apart: the required form with `topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname` and a `labelSelector` matching the pod's own label forces replicas onto **different** nodes. The scheduler won't co-locate two matching pods on one host.

**Gotcha:** if replicas exceed available nodes, the extra pods stay `Pending` — hard anti-affinity can't double up on a host.
questions.prompt:
In `sched-learn` create a 2-replica Deployment `spread` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`, pod label `app=spread`) with **required** podAntiAffinity on `topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname` matching `app=spread`, tolerating any taint.

Target: both `spread` replicas are `Running` on **different** nodes via required podAntiAffinity.
questions.hint: `affinity.podAntiAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: [{labelSelector: {matchLabels: {app: spread}}, topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname}]`; add `tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]` so both nodes are usable.
questions.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: spread
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: spread
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: spread
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - operator: Exists
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - labelSelector:
              matchLabels:
                app: spread
            topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
      containers:
      - name: c
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: spread: 2 replicas Running on 2 distinct nodes via required podAntiAffinity

questions.eli5:
Picture a company that puts its two backup generators in **different** buildings on purpose — if one building loses power, the other generator keeps running. Putting identical things far apart so a single failure can't take them all out: that's **podAntiAffinity**.

Normal affinity *attracts* a pod to certain nodes. Anti-affinity does the opposite among **pods**: it tells the scheduler "don't put me next to a pod that looks like *this*." Here the rule is "don't place me on a node that already has a pod labeled `app=spread`." Since every replica carries `app=spread`, each one repels the others — so the two replicas end up on two different nodes.

The magic word is **`topologyKey`**. It defines what "next to" means. With `topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname`, "together" means "same node," so the rule spreads pods one-per-node. (Point it at a zone label instead and it spreads one-per-zone.)

Like node affinity, it has a **required** (hard) form and a **preferred** (soft) one. You're using the hard form, so the scheduler will flat-out refuse to double up.

**Watch out:**

- **More replicas than nodes = `Pending` leftovers.** Hard anti-affinity can't put two matching pods on one host, so if you ask for 3 replicas on a 2-node cluster, one stays stuck. Use the *preferred* form if you'd rather they double up than wait.
- **`topologyKey` is mandatory** and defines the spread domain. `kubernetes.io/hostname` = per node.
- The **`labelSelector` must match the pods' own labels** (`app=spread`) — point it at the wrong label and nothing repels anything.
- Don't confuse it with `nodeAntiAffinity` — there's no such field. "Keep off nodes" uses nodeAffinity with `NotIn`; "keep away from pods" uses podAntiAffinity.
- Tainted nodes still need a toleration to count as usable spread targets.
questions.deepDive:
## Pod anti-affinity (spread) — full rundown

### The one-sentence model
**podAffinity attracts pods toward other pods; podAntiAffinity repels them apart — both scoped by a `topologyKey`.** The required form with `topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname` forces one matching pod per node.

### Where it lives
```yaml
spec:
  affinity:
    podAntiAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: spread
        topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
```
For a Deployment this goes in `spec.template.spec`.

### The three ingredients of every pod (anti)affinity term
| Field | Meaning | Required? |
|---|---|---|
| `labelSelector` | which *other pods* to match (via `matchLabels`/`matchExpressions`) | yes |
| `topologyKey` | node label that defines the "domain" (what counts as co-located) | **yes** |
| `namespaces` / `namespaceSelector` | which namespaces the matched pods live in (default: the pod's own namespace) | no |

### topologyKey — the heart of it
`topologyKey` names a **node label**. Two nodes with the same value for that label are in the same "topology domain."

| topologyKey | Domain = | Anti-affinity spreads across |
|---|---|---|
| `kubernetes.io/hostname` | one node | nodes (one pod per node) |
| `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` | one zone | zones (one pod per zone) |
| `topology.kubernetes.io/region` | one region | regions |

For anti-affinity: "don't schedule me where a matching pod already exists **in the same topology domain**."

### Required vs preferred
| | required | preferred |
|---|---|---|
| Field | `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` | `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` |
| Shape | **list of terms** (each: `labelSelector` + `topologyKey`) | list of `{weight, podAffinityTerm}` |
| No valid spot → | pod `Pending` | pod schedules anyway (doubling up allowed) |

> Note the shape difference from nodeAffinity: pod anti-affinity's *required* form is already a **list of terms** (no `nodeSelectorTerms` wrapper). The *preferred* form wraps each term in `podAffinityTerm` with a `weight`.

### podAffinity vs podAntiAffinity
- **podAffinity** — co-locate: "put me WITH pods matching X" (e.g. app next to its cache).
- **podAntiAffinity** — spread: "keep me AWAY from pods matching X" (HA / fault tolerance).
Both use the same `labelSelector` + `topologyKey` structure.

### Worked example (2 replicas, 2 nodes)
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: { name: spread, namespace: sched-learn }
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: spread } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: spread } }
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - { operator: Exists }
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - labelSelector:
              matchLabels: { app: spread }
            topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
      containers:
      - { name: c, image: busybox:1.36, command: ["sleep","3600"] }
```
Replica 1 lands anywhere; replica 2 is repelled from replica 1's node → different node.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **replicas > eligible nodes → extras `Pending`.** Hard anti-affinity cannot double up. `describe` shows *"node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules."* Switch to the preferred form to allow stacking.
- **`topologyKey` is mandatory** — omitting it is invalid. It must be a label present on the nodes.
- **`labelSelector` must target the pods you want spread** (usually the template's own label). A mismatched selector silently does nothing.
- **Namespace scope**: pod affinity matches pods in the **same namespace by default**; use `namespaces:`/`namespaceSelector:` to widen.
- There is **no `nodeAntiAffinity`** field. Keep-off-a-node = nodeAffinity with `NotIn`/`DoesNotExist`.
- Anti-affinity is **relatively expensive** to evaluate at scale; `topologySpreadConstraints` is the lighter, modern alternative for even spreading.
- Still ignores taints — tainted spread targets need a toleration.

### Quick reference
```yaml
affinity:
  podAntiAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    - labelSelector:
        matchLabels: { app: spread }
      topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
```
```bash
kubectl -n sched-learn get pods -l app=spread -o wide   # each on a distinct NODE
kubectl -n sched-learn rollout status deploy/spread
```
